manual.machine_interface.line2: {0}With the increasing complexity of multiblock machinery, keeping track of their needs becomes quite complex.{1}
manual.machine_interface.line3: While {0}comparator signals{1} can provide some insight into the amount of items inside, only the Machine Interface can provide a more detailed evaluation and send redstone signals.{2}
manual.machine_interface.line4: When placed against the redstone control surface of a multiblock, opening the GUI will allow setting up a variety of conditions by which to output a signal.{0}
manual.machine_interface.line5: Press the "Add Condition" button to add a new row. Within that row, the first button serves to delete it again, the second one is for configuring the signal color to output on.{0}
manual.machine_interface.line6: This is followed by two dropdown menus, one for selecting the type of check (such as "Machine Active", "Item Input", "Fluid Output") and one for selecting the condition.{0}
manual.machine_interface.line7: Most checks support "Comparator Output" for a signal strength that is scaled to the items/fluid/energy stored. There also exists various from true or false options, such as "75% Filled" or "Empty".{0}
manual.machine_interface.line8: As soon as a condition is matched, the Machine Interface will output the relevant signal on the configured color-channel to any attached {0}Redstone Interface Connector{1}.{2}
manual.machine_interface.line9: In addition to sending, the Machine Interface can also receive a redstone signal and output it to the connected machine. The signal color for that is configured in the bottom right of the GUI.{0}
manual.machine_interface.line10: This allows for use of the {0}Logic Unit{1} to evaluate the signals coming from the machine and then send one back to enable or disable it!
